title: Conveyor demo
description: Small program with live values you can watch in the simulator.

title: TwinCAT ADS
description: Beckhoff ADS starter. Simulates now; connect the PLC later.

title: Raspberry Pi (EtherCAT / GPIO)
description: Pi EtherCAT/GPIO starter. Simulates now; connect I/O later.

title: HMI starter

title: PLCopen Motion
description: Single-axis motion starter. Runs in the simulator.

title: 1. Control-loop elements
description: Identify setpoint, controlled variable, measurement, actuator and command. Establish the physical response direction through a manual experiment.

title: 2. ON/OFF control
description: Repeatedly compare temperature with the setpoint and switch refrigeration. Write the comparison and decision in ST.

title: 3. Hysteresis and dwell
description: Retain switching state between thresholds and postpone transitions until minimum ON/OFF times have elapsed.

title: 4. Cold-room commissioning
description: Write and assess the complete binary controller, including changed heat load, temperature variation, switching frequency and reset behavior.

title: 5. Proportional control
description: Calculate heater output from error. Observe how output decreases as temperature approaches the setpoint.

title: 6. PI control
description: Accumulate error over time and add the stored integral contribution to P. Demonstrate removal of the same steady-state error observed previously.

title: 7. Saturation and windup
description: Explain actuator capacity, unreachable setpoints and continued integral accumulation during saturation. Observe delayed recovery after returning to a feasible setpoint.

title: 8. Anti-windup
description: Derive applied-output tracking, explain its correction direction and compare recovery from the same saturation event.

title: 9. Setpoint and disturbance response
description: Distinguish a setpoint change from a physical load change. Set requirements for overshoot, temperature excursion, settling and output use before testing.

title: 10. Loop diagnosis
description: Check measurement credibility, command delivery, actuator behavior, operating conditions and feasibility before changing gains.

title: 11. Manual PI tuning
description: Choose a bounded gain change, predict its effect, repeat matched experiments and keep or reject the new settings.

title: 12. Process dynamics
description: Identify which equilibrium and dynamic predictions would improve the next tuning decision. Explain why a closed-loop trace is not a direct plant measurement.

title: 13. Energy balance
description: Derive temperature dynamics from heat capacity, delivered power, heat loss and delay. Explain units, assumptions and operating-point deviations.

title: 14. Identification experiments
description: Choose operating point, command step, duration, measurement conditions and stopping limits. Establish a repeatable baseline and retain the applied-input record.

title: 15. Step-response identification
description: Estimate gain, time constant and delay. Distinguish detectable onset from physical delay and explain uncertainty in the estimates.

title: 16. Model structure
description: Compare simple and extended models. Derive an additional sensor or process state from its physical operation rather than adding an unexplained fitting parameter.

title: 17. Identifiability
description: Explain practical and structural parameter ambiguity. Choose additional excitation, longer observation or an independent measurement for a specific reason.

title: 18. Model validation
description: Assess timing, response shape and final value on independent command and disturbance records. Decide whether the model supports the intended design decision.

title: 19. Model-based PI tuning
description: Derive starting gains from the validated model and a chosen response time. Retain relevant delay, additional dynamics and uncertainty.

title: 20. Relay tuning
description: Produce and measure a repeatable bounded cycle. Explain the approximation and empirical rule used to calculate candidate settings.

title: 21. Tuning comparison
description: Compare manual, model-based and relay-derived candidates. Assess every requirement before choosing between qualifying settings. Allow none to qualify.

title: 22. Setpoint weighting
description: Separate setpoint and measurement contributions to P while retaining full error in I. Assess reduced command steps against slower response.

title: 23. Measurement filtering
description: Derive a filter update and compare noise reduction with delayed detection of real temperature changes. Distinguish raw, filtered and physical values.

title: 24. Sampling and timing
description: Explain aliasing, acquisition timestamps, controller intervals and held commands. Scale integral and filter updates correctly and reject unusable timing.

title: 25. Controller initialization
description: Introduce persistent controller instances, inputs, parameters, outputs and retained state. Initialize integral, filter and timing values deliberately.

title: 26. Bumpless transfer
description: Align the integral with manual output and current proportional action. Assess the transfer-induced command change separately from later temperature response.

title: 27. Parameter updates
description: Validate and apply a complete parameter set at one update boundary. Preserve intended state continuity and distinguish deliberate limit changes from accidental jumps.

title: 28. Measurement validity
description: Detect unusable data, select the defined output response, preserve appropriate state and require fresh measurements before restarting automatic control.

title: 29. Heater commissioning
description: Write the ST integration and assess setpoint response, disturbance recovery, startup, transfer, limits, parameter changes and measurement faults.

title: 30. Actuator tracking
description: Distinguish requested position, bounded target and measured position. Explain rate-limit windup and correct integral state using actual actuator position.

title: 31. Valve characteristics
description: Explain and measure how valve position, pressure drop and pipe losses determine flow. Convert flow into heating at stated temperatures.

title: 32. Valve stiction
description: Diagnose deadband, holding force, breakaway and sticking through command, position, force and flow observations. Separate mechanical problems from tuning problems.

title: 33. Position control
description: Introduce shaft angle, velocity, torque, inertia and friction. Apply proportional position feedback and explain continued motion at zero position error.

title: 34. PD control
description: Calculate braking torque from measured velocity. Explain damping, derivative on measurement and setpoint-induced derivative kick.

title: 35. PID load rejection
description: Calculate the torque from one explicit constant load. Compare PD steady error with PID recovery and account for torque saturation.

title: 36. Derivative filtering
description: Explain noise amplification in a finite-difference velocity estimate. Filter it and assess both torque movement and delayed braking.

title: 37. Discrete PID
description: Calculate P, trial I, filtered D, requested output, output limiting and tracking for one update. Identify old and new values explicitly.

title: 38. Positional and incremental PID
description: Derive output increments from consecutive complete-output equations. Preserve the state and correction terms required for equivalent behavior.

title: 39. Servo commissioning
description: Write and assess positioning, constant-load rejection, torque limits, initialization, transfer and fault recovery on the same shaft.

title: 40. Volume balance
description: Derive level rate from inflow, outflow and tank area. Explain why equal flows preserve the current level rather than restore a previous level.

title: 41. Gravity outflow
description: Derive the square-root flow relationship and combine it with volume storage. Explain level-dependent equilibrium and response speed.

title: 42. Linearization
description: Derive a tangent approximation, local gain and time constant. Quantify errors for small and larger departures from the operating point.

title: 43. Gain scheduling
description: Calculate scheduled PI settings from the local tank model. Preserve controller state and compare scheduled and fixed gains across operating levels.

title: 44. Laplace transforms
description: Transform physical equations, retain initial-condition contributions and connect transfer functions. Solve the simple heater response and present more complicated familiar response expressions.

title: 45. Poles and zeros
description: Define poles and zeros before using them. Explain decay, growth, oscillation, input-response shape and specific cancellation examples through heater and shaft behavior.

title: 46. Characteristic equations
description: Derive the equation governing natural modes from plant dynamics and the actual feedback law. Account for feedback signs, controller state and possible cancellation.

title: 47. Root locus
description: Vary one gain while holding the other controller and plant properties fixed. Relate pole movement to damping and response speed.

title: 48. Routh–Hurwitz stability
description: Construct and interpret the Routh table. Find a stable gain interval and distinguish stable, marginal and unstable boundary cases.

title: 49. Periodic excitation
description: Choose a bounded sinusoidal input, operating point, frequency, amplitude and observation duration. Exclude startup transients and retain actual applied signals.

title: 50. Frequency response
description: Derive sinusoidal response, introduce complex magnitude and angle, and interpret Bode plots with meaningful units and references.

title: 51. Sensitivity functions
description: Derive sensitivity and complementary sensitivity. Trace disturbances and noise into physical output and controller command, retaining the correct physical input paths.

title: 52. Loop shaping
description: Derive and implement lead/lag compensation. Assess the complete loop, noise amplification, actuator demand and temperature performance under fixed requirements.

title: 53. Nyquist stability
description: Explain the critical point, directed curve, pole count and encirclements. Determine how delivery delay changes stability and interpret slow growth near the boundary.

title: 54. Sampled-data stability
description: Derive held-command state updates and include the pending command. Explain unit-circle stability and separate physical timing from numerical integration errors.

title: 55. Feedforward control
description: Derive a disturbance-based command from physical balance. Combine it with feedback and assess measurement error, limits and delivery delay.

title: 56. Cascade control
description: Explain outer and inner loops, their different output quantities, relative response speeds, initialization and tracking. Assess earlier jacket-disturbance correction.

title: 57. Ratio control
description: Calculate and regulate an additive-to-carrier ratio. Account for pump lag, invalid measurements, low carrier flow and residual delivery after stopping.

title: 58. Split-range control
description: Convert net heat demand into appropriately scaled heater and cooler commands. Explain service exclusion, neutral regions and tracking from applied net heat.

title: 59. Override control
description: Select between normal and limiting requests, track inactive controllers and distinguish incompatible requirements from poor tuning.

title: 60. Smith prediction
description: Combine delay-free and delayed model predictions with current measurement correction. Assess model mismatch and transfer to ordinary feedback when prediction is unsuitable.

title: 61. Vessel commissioning
description: Select and assess suitable single-loop, cascade, split-range or override arrangements. Keep physical assumptions and requirements fixed across candidates.

title: 62. Multivariable process paths
description: Derive coupled balances and measure each actuator's effect on each output. Introduce the gain matrix through its scalar physical relationships.

title: 63. Relative gain array
description: Derive isolated and compensated gains. Explain inverse, transpose and elementwise operations through the physical pairing calculation.

title: 64. Decentralized PI
description: Use separate PI states for paired loops. Assess changed and unchanged outputs under both setpoint directions and disturbance locations.

title: 65. Static decoupling
description: Derive the virtual-to-physical command map, holding biases and correct tracking through physical limits. Compare steady cancellation and transient costs.

title: 66. Multivariable design selection
description: Compare fixed architectures under unchanged requirements and justified uncertainty cases. Separate feasibility, transient performance and evidence coverage.

title: 67. State-space models
description: Derive the two-tank state equations from storage balances. Explain states, inputs, outputs and matrix rows through physical quantities and units.

title: 68. Controllability
description: Explain reachable local transient states and the controllability calculation. Distinguish transient reachability from independently maintainable steady setpoints.

title: 69. Observability
description: Derive how downstream level and its change reveal upstream state. Explain why noisy differentiation can be practically unreliable despite theoretical observability.

title: 70. State feedback
description: Calculate a pump correction from both level deviations. Derive gains from chosen closed-loop modes and assess actuator limits and local-model validity.

title: 71. State observers
description: Derive model prediction plus innovation correction. Choose observer gains, preserve update order and assess convergence and noise sensitivity.

title: 72. Kalman filtering
description: Define variance and covariance, derive weighting and perform a complete prediction/correction calculation. Compare estimated error with evaluation truth.

title: 73. LQR control
description: Derive costs from physical scales. Explain one-step minimization, future cost, backward calculation and the resulting finite-horizon feedback gains.

title: 74. LQG control
description: Explain the assumptions behind combining LQR and Kalman filtering. Integrate prediction, correction and control using the previous applied input.

title: 75. Model predictive control
description: Predict over a stated horizon, evaluate explicit costs and constraints, apply the first selected command and replan. Distinguish planning failure from insufficient capacity.

title: 76. Lyapunov stability
description: Derive an energy-like function for the nonlinear arm, explain its rate of change and establish a region consistent with actuator limits.

title: 77. Feedback linearization
description: Derive nonlinear compensation from physical forces. Distinguish exact model cancellation from local approximation and assess coefficient error, noise and limits.

title: 78. Adaptive control
description: Derive parameter estimation, state its information requirements and qualify updates before changing tuning. Compare adapted and fixed settings on the same physical condition.

title: 79. Robust control
description: Define bounded model uncertainty, check feasibility and distinguish robust stability from robust performance. Explain finite tests and range-wide bounds.

title: 80. Networked control
description: Handle sequence, connection identity, command age, clock assumptions, finite holding, local fallback and deliberate remote recovery.

title: 81. Fault-aware control
description: Distinguish range, age and disagreement faults. Implement justified sensor fallback, state alignment, fault latching and qualified recovery.

title: 82. Independent design
description: Define requirements, select two suitable designs, calculate feasibility, write their ST integrations and defend the choice using matched performance, uncertainty and recovery evidence.
